note: Append-only. Grants no authority and authorizes no stage. Must be approved and hash-bound into the bridge-canary and main-run manifests BEFORE either runs: a disposition chosen after the outcomes are visible is not a policy.
why_this_exists: The frozen protocol already settles what happens to a cell that produces a bad verdict, and the canary confirmed those paths work. What it does not settle is a cell that produces NO row at all. The 2026-07-28 canary had five such cells (four terminal checker halts and one dependent), against a completion_policy of '100% exact provider-cell completion'. Deciding their disposition after the fact would make exclusions depend on which cells happened to fail, and cells fail non-uniformly across conditions and models, so post-hoc dropping is a condition-dependent filter wearing the costume of housekeeping.

invalid_verdict.rule: strict INVALID counts wrong; valid-only sensitivity
invalid_verdict.canary_evidence: 10 of 792 comparable rows (1.3%) failed the strict parser; 9 were b0 cells where the judge emitted an oracle query or an empty string instead of a verdict, from gpt-oss-120b or gemma.

never_regenerate_a_bad_verdict.rule: query-screen retry only; never regenerate an invalid verdict
never_regenerate_a_bad_verdict.consequence: an unparseable verdict is a permanent property of the cell, not a transient to be retried away. This is what stops retries selecting for parseable answers.

transport_retry.rule: repeat identical request and seed; conservatively charge until provider reconciliation
transport_retry.consequence: transport failures are retried byte-identically and cannot change what is sampled; semantic outputs are never retried. The two must not be conflated.

matched_side_assignment.rule: K2 mirrored; labels fixed across matched conditions
matched_side_assignment.consequence: a batch replay must present the same answer at Position A as the sequential cell it replays. The executor now refuses a mismatch rather than producing an incomparable pair.

blocked_and_exhausted_queries_are_not_mi.rule: a rejected query and an exhausted budget are the gate working as frozen, not failures
blocked_and_exhausted_queries_are_not_mi.canary_evidence: of 813 gate events, 134 blocked and 319 exhausted; 57 were rejected mechanically before reaching the checker, which the contract prescribes for patterns P1 and P2.

the_gap_this_closes.case: a planned cell that produces no result row after the frozen allowances are exhausted
observed_causes: checker_malformed: the frozen checker returns a response the frozen parser cannot read. The per-call cache memoises it, so every resume replays the same unparseable response and the cell can never complete. Four occurrences in roughly 1,500 canary checker calls (0.27%).
dependency_terminally_halted: a cell whose parent terminally halted. One occurrence.

reviewer unreachable at the frozen failure rule, which commits non-ALLOW rather than leaving a cell incomplete, so this does NOT produce a missing row and is listed only to be excluded from this category.

proposed_rule.1_no_silent_exclusion: Every planned cell appears in the reported distributions. A cell with no result row is reported under its terminal outcome (checker_malformed, dependency_terminally_halted), never omitted from denominators.
proposed_rule.2_incomplete_counts_as_invalid: For the primary estimands, a cell that cannot produce a verdict after the frozen allowances counts INVALID, and INVALID counts wrong. This is the same direction as the already-frozen invalid_policy, applies identically in every condition, and is conservative: it can only attenuate an effect, never manufacture one.
proposed_rule.3_the_sensitivity_is_pre-declared: The valid-only sensitivity already required by invalid_policy is computed on the same support, dropping incomplete cells from every arm at once rather than per-arm.
proposed_rule.4_identity_preserved_on_common_support: H, P and R are computed on identical weighting and identical cell support inside every bootstrap replicate, so H = P + R holds exactly. A batch parent that fails must remove its whole matched set from all three estimands, never give P a different population from R.
proposed_rule.5_differential_incompletion_is_a_reporte: Incompletion is tabulated per condition, per judge and per world, and reported whether or not it crosses any threshold.

proposed_ex_ante_gates.note: THESE NUMBERS ARE THE PROPOSAL AND NEED OWNER SIGN-OFF. They are calibrated on the canary's observed 0.27% terminal-halt rate and are otherwise a judgement call, which is exactly why they must be fixed before the run rather than after.
proposed_ex_ante_gates.overall_incompletion_ceiling: 1.0% of planned cells. Above this the run is reported as incomplete and the primary is not treated as answering the pre-registered question.
proposed_ex_ante_gates.differential_incompletion_ceiling: 0.5 percentage points between the highest and lowest of the three primary conditions (b0, sequential_b2, batch_same_qa_b2). Above this the primary is flagged compromised and the valid-only sensitivity becomes the headline, because differential missingness across exactly the conditions being differenced is the failure mode that would masquerade as an effect.
proposed_ex_ante_gates.batch_parent_loss_ceiling: 1.0% of batch_same_qa_b2 cells losing their sequential parent. This is called out separately because it is the one loss that attacks P and R together while leaving H untouched.

what_this_does_not_decide: the retry allowances themselves, which are frozen in decisions.execution_semantics and unchanged here
whether the main run proceeds at all
anything about the 2026-07-28 canary's own five excluded cells, whose disposition is recorded in its close-out
